snippet.title: Meta Employees AI Training Data
snippet.description:
How Meta is turning its employees into AI training data

🖱️ Meta is installing tracking software on employees’ work computers to capture mouse movements, clicks, keystrokes, and occasional screen snapshots.  

🤖 The goal isn’t performance monitoring (per Meta), it’s to generate real human “computer-use” training data so AI agents can learn to operate apps and interfaces.  

⚖️ In the U.S., there’s little federal restriction on this kind of workplace monitoring; state laws mainly require disclosure, so it’s broadly legal even if the optics are rough.

snippet.title: Unfortunately, You Need to Know What the Jevons Paradox is
snippet.description:
One thing I think a lot AI boosters get wrong is that they think AI will be good at creating new, quality information while, at the moment, the only thing it has shown utility at is organizing existing information. Even the weights themselves are a kind of distillation of existing information. 

Much of science...perhaps even the great majority of it, is not organizing existing information, it is acquiring new information. AI might make that more efficient, but it does not do it. 

This is one of the things that writing this video made me think. I look forward to other people's thoughts in the comments.
